Performers
Bidú Sayão (soprano), Leonard Rose (solo cello), Eight cellos and double bass (players not named) (ensemble), Heitor Villa-⁠Lobos (conductor) Documented

Both label scans read “BIDÚ SAYÃO (Soprano) with Eight ’Celli and Bass conducted by Heitor Villa-⁠Lobos; Solo ’Cello: Leonard Rose”. The Internet Archive description gives the same names.

[2] [1]
Work version
First movement only, for soprano and an orchestra of cellos, in the form of 1938; sung in Portuguese. Documented

The Columbia labels give the movement as “Aria – Cantilena”, in two parts marked “Beginning” and “Conclusion”, and read “Sung in Portuguese”. The Dansa (Martelo) was added in 1945 and is not on this disc.

[2] [4]
Recorded
1945 (year only) Inferred, not documented

The Internet Archive item dates the recording 1945. The record appears in the Columbia catalogue of 1946, and a New Yorker profile places Villa-⁠Lobos in New York in February 1945. No session date is stated in the sources consulted.

[1] [3] [5]
Place
Unknown Unknown

No recording location is stated on the labels or in the Internet Archive description.

Label
Columbia Masterworks (United States) Documented

The labels read “Columbia Masterworks … Made in U.S.A.”.

[2]
Catalogue
71670-D, 12-inch 78 rpm; listed in the Columbia catalogues of 1946 and 1947 Documented

The 1946 catalogue lists “Bachiana Brasileira No. 5 (Villa-⁠Lobos)” with Bidú Sayão and an orchestra conducted by Villa-⁠Lobos at 71670-D; the 1947 catalogue lists it at the same number with a price of 1.00.

[2] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Side one, “(Beginning)”: XCO 34194; side two, “(Conclusion)”: XCO 34195. Take numbers are not shown. Documented

Read from the two label scans in the Internet Archive item.

[2]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The item was uploaded by a private account in the Internet Archive’s hifidelity collection. No transfer engineer is named, and the account name is not reproduced here.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item’s public date, 10 March 2025, is the date of upload, not of the transfer.

[1]
Processing
Per the uploader: equalisation with a 300 Hz bass turnover and a treble roll-off, and de-clicking with iZotope RX10; the original file is a WAV and the site’s stream is the Internet Archive MP3 derivative. Documented

The two disc sides are run together in one file. The source disc copy and the playback equipment are not described.

[1]
Composition rights
Villa-⁠Lobos died in 1959, so the work is in copyright in the EU, under the life-plus-70 term, until the end of 2029. IMSLP records it as public domain in Canada and in life-plus-50 countries and as probably still protected in the United States; its first publication was in 1947 (Associated Music Publishers). Documented

Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording. This dossier does not assert that the composition is free of copyright.

[4]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963 (Columbia 71670-D, listed in the 1946 catalogue). Documented

The 1946 catalogue is a dated witness that the disc was on sale by then; the exact release date is not established. The Internet Archive item carries a CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 label chosen by the uploader, which is not relied on here. The United States status of a recording first published in 1945 or 1946 is not established.

[3] [2]

Heitor Villa-⁠Lobos, Bachianas Brasileiras No. 5, I. Ária (Cantilena). Bidú Sayão, soprano; Leonard Rose, solo cello; eight cellos and double bass; Heitor Villa-⁠Lobos, conductor. Columbia Masterworks 71670-D (matrices XCO 34194–⁠34195), recorded 1945, issued by 1946. Internet Archive item bachianas-brasileiras-no.-5 (uploader’s transfer). Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established. Rights statement
